question: Who classified Indian society into seven classes?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Megasthenes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Indica was written by Megasthenese, who was a Greek ambassador sent to the court of Chandragupta Maurya by Seleucus Nicator.
 
• Megasthenese through Indica states that Indian society was divided into 7 social classes:
 
 
• Philosophers
 
• Farmers
 
• Soldiers
 
• Herdsmen
 
• Artisans
 
• Magistrates
 
• Councilors
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Kautilya’s Arthshastra is the most important literary source for the Mauryas.​

 
 
• It gives a clear and methodological analysis of the political and economic conditions of the Mauryan period.
 
• It looked up to Shudras as an Aryan community which is distinguished from Malechha or non-Aryan communities.
 
 
 
• **Strabo **is best known for his work Geographica ("Geography"), which presented a descriptive history of people and places from different regions of the world known during his lifetime.
 
• **Pliny**- His most famous work, however, was “Historia Naturalis” (Natural History), an encyclopedia of natural science that spanned thirty-seven books.
 
• Puranas though are a collection of legends inter-spread with religious teachings, they give us the chronology and lists of Mauryan Kings.
 
• Mudra Rakshasa was written by Vishakha Dutta during the Gupta Period, but it describes how Chandragupta Maurya get Chanakya's assistance to overthrow the Nandas
